subject: Math
prompt: The equation $V(h) = 120(Q)^\frac{h}{6}$ gives the predicted value $V(h)$, in thousands of dollars, of an investment $h$ hours after the initial measurement, where $Q$ is a constant greater than $1$. The predicted value increases by $p%$ every $120$ minutes. What is the value of $p$ in terms of $Q$?
explanation: Choice A is correct. The percentage increase $p$ can be found by evaluating the function at the beginning and end of the time interval, finding the ratio, and applying the percentage increase formula $p = 100(\text{ratio} - 1)$. First, convert the time interval to hours: $120$ minutes equals $\frac{120}{60} = 2$ hours. At the initial time ($h = 0$), the value is $V(0) = 120(Q)^{\frac{0}{6}} = 120(Q)^0 = 120$ thousand dollars. After $2$ hours ($h = 2$), the value is $V(2) = 120(Q)^{\frac{2}{6}} = 120(Q)^{\frac{1}{3}}$ thousand dollars. The ratio of the new value to the initial value is $\frac{V(2)}{V(0)} = \frac{120(Q)^{\frac{1}{3}}}{120} = Q^{\frac{1}{3}}$. The percentage increase formula is $p = 100(\text{ratio} - 1)$, which gives $p = 100(Q^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1)$. Therefore, the value of $p$ in terms of $Q$ is $100(Q^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1)$.
